idiom_name: HttpRoutes[F] => HttpRoutes[F] applied to the routes
implementation_notes: http4s makes the chain a function on the service type - HttpRoutes[F] => HttpRoutes[F], a Kleisli transformation - so composition replaces the FilterManager: the middleware is applied to the routes and post-processing is a map over the effectful response. The library ships the common filters (RequestLogger, Metrics, Timeout, ErrorHandling, CORS) and HttpApp closes the chain with orNotFound. This is the default for effect-typed Scala services.
code_sketch:
def addRequestId[F[_]: Sync](routes: HttpRoutes[F]): HttpRoutes[F] =
  Kleisli { req =>                                            // pre
    val id = req.headers.get(ci"X-Request-Id").fold(UUID.randomUUID().toString)(_.head.value)
    routes.run(req.putHeaders(Header.Raw(ci"X-Request-Id", id)))   // inner routes
      .map(_.map(_.putHeaders(Header.Raw(ci"X-Traced", "true"))))  // post
  }
val app: HttpApp[IO] = addRequestId(routes).orNotFound
pitfalls: The wrapped service must be run inside the effect: a middleware that returns the function without flatMapping the response never executes the post path.
HttpRoutes yields OptionT[F, Response], so a filter that ignores the Option can turn a legitimate 404 into an unhandled None.
Composition order is inside-out: with addRequestId(metrics(routes)) the outermost middleware is the one applied last.

variants.name: Play filters (EssentialFilter over EssentialAction)
variants.implementation_notes: Play realizes the chain with objects: EssentialFilter wraps an EssentialAction, so the filter receives the next action and returns one whose Accumulator it can map, compose with a Pekko Streams flow, or abandon to block the request; the simpler Filter trait extends EssentialFilter by building that wrapper for you. Filters are registered through HttpFilters (or DefaultHttpFilters) and are intended for concerns applied to every route - route-specific concerns belong in action composition instead. Choose this variant inside a Play HTTP server rather than an effect-typed http4s application.
pitfalls: EssentialAction works on the request body as a stream: materialising or replaying it in a filter breaks Content-Length or consumes the body for later stages.
Filters run after routing, so they cannot rewrite the path or method to influence route selection - that requires an HttpRequestHandler.
Play's default filter set already enforces security headers; adding a second enforcement filter duplicates work and can conflict on headers.
